text: <blocked>The unit's bad() takes no arguments and its body unconditionally allocates only 10 bytes via alloca(10), then casts that pointer to int* and writes 10 ints (40 bytes) through it in a fixed loop, overflowing the allocation by 30 bytes on every single call regardless of any driver input. There is no safe argument or calling strategy that avoids this since bad() is niladic and the overflow is unconditional; AddressSanitizer's default redzone instrumentation for alloca'd stack memory will flag this as a stack-buffer-overflow the moment bad() executes. Since the ABI contract mandates calling bad() (many times) and the driver must remain sanitizer-clean, no driver.c satisfying both requirements can be written for this unit.</blocked>
